headline: TOMORROW IS THE HEAVIEST MONDAY ON THIS BOARD IN WEEKS — the 225 Willow Point shoot, the 198 Rena reinstatement decision and the Lake Crest closing confirmation all land inside 24 hours, while the agent whose buyers put 355 Comanche at the top of their list has now been uncalled for nineteen hours. · DO: call Amy G. tonight · WATCH: Make credits pause the whole automation layer around Thursday.

notes: ✅ A FULL SUNDAY OF ON-TIME PASSES, NOTHING BLOCKED, AND THE NO-TOUCH RULE HELD END TO END — roughly twenty-five sweeps since midnight, zero sends, zero drafts, zero texts by construction. That is the rule working, not the lane going dark. The morning letter fired at 6:45, the midday digest at 12:30, and the evening sweep at 6:15 caught net-new signal rather than coasting. ⭐ The one item this board opened the day demanding — the photographer for tomorrow's shoot — closed at 12:14 on your word, both halves of it.

🆕 THE EVENING SWEEP WAS THE MOST PRODUCTIVE PASS OF THE DAY, AND IT WAS ALL SELLER SIGNAL. Three fresh owner hand-raises landed after midday: two homeowners who told your site your own estimate on their house was TOO LOW — the single highest-intent shape a home-value lead takes, because it is an owner arguing about their own number — and one buyer who came off the 19-lot ad and then registered on the IDX site four minutes later. All three are queued for a verified 7 AM Monday first touch rather than sent blind on a Sunday. ⭐ The desk also stood one stale item DOWN with a written reason rather than letting it age quietly, which is the healthier half of a good sweep.

⚠️ TWO HOUSEKEEPING FINDINGS, BOTH SMALL, BOTH REAL — a duplicate call task was created for the same person twice today under two slightly different name spellings, which is the exact twin the dedupe rule exists to prevent, and it is flagged here rather than silently absorbed. 🛑 Separately and unchanged: the automation platform is 75% through its credit cycle and every scenario on it pauses when the meter runs dry, projected around Thursday with no renewal until roughly the 30th. That is the instant-lead alert and the send path for these briefings, dark for about nine days.

callBlock.who: Amy G. of Ethos International — her buyers put 355 Comanche TOP OF THEIR LIST, and she is still uncalled
callBlock.why: 🔥 STILL THE HOTTEST THING ON THIS BOARD AND IT IS NOW NINETEEN HOURS OLD. She filed at 11:24 last night: interested — YES, and in her own words her buyers have just started looking, really like the property, and have put it at the top of their list. ⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER YES ON THIS HOUSE: she is the same agent who phoned you from inside the home mid-showing on Saturday, and you already answered half of what she asked by text. The channel is open and warm — this is a returned call, not a cold approach. ⚠️ THE HALF YOU DID NOT ANSWER IS THE PROBLEM: she reported the basement lights would not come on, and it is still open. Buyers who have 'just started looking' will tour more houses this week, and the last thing they saw in yours was a dark basement. ⏰ A Sunday-evening call still beats a Monday one — they are deciding what to see next as the weekend ends. ⭐ She also left BOTH price fields blank and scored staging a 3 — the only agent to score staging since the cut, so ask her what she would change.

callBlock.who: Thomas D. — he said YES on Friday, and the document he asked for now exists
callBlock.why: ✅ THIS IS THE ONE THAT UNBLOCKED ITSELF. He replied "Yes" Friday morning and asked for the White Tail Run lot layout and the per-acre number. 🆕 THE 19-LOT PLAT WAS LOCATED THE SAME MORNING and emailed — the exact deliverable his open chip had been waiting on. ⭐ SO THE CALL IS NO LONGER A HOLDING REPLY, IT IS A FOLLOW-UP ON SOMETHING HE ALREADY HAS, which is a completely different conversation. 🔥 He is one of six names off the 19-lot ad, and that ad remains the only advertising in the portfolio producing anything at all — a seventh name came off it this afternoon. ⏰ Two days since he answered; the gap between 'he said yes' and 'nobody called' is where this one dies.

callBlock.who: Chesley C. — five days unreturned, mid-transaction, on the cleanest deal you have
callBlock.why: ⚠️ THE ODD PART IS WHO THIS IS — not a cold lead but the seller on the file this board calls the cleanest in the book, with the inspection and the appraisal both already spent and the close receipted for 8/28. ⭐ A CLIENT MID-TRANSACTION WHO CALLS AND GETS NOTHING BACK IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE SILENCE YOU CAN BUY, because it costs the referral rather than the closing. ✅ ONE THING ON THIS FILE WENT RIGHT WITHOUT YOU THIS WEEK: your operations manager chased and closed the payoff item on 8/14, which is the catch that protects the 8/28 close. ⚠️ There is still live business on the same call: the appraised value has not come back at day ten, and the buyer's agent asked for a specific co-op commission that nobody has ever answered. All of it is one phone call, not three. ⭐ Monday is Client Day — this is exactly the row it exists for.

callBlock.who: Gloria F. — the tenant answer is now twenty-three days owed
callBlock.why: 🔴 THE LONGEST-RUNNING BROKEN PROMISE ON THE BOARD. She waited nineteen days without complaining, then escalated three times in twenty-seven minutes on Wednesday night — two voicemails and a text. ✅ THE EMERGENCY HALF RESOLVED WITHOUT YOU: power is back on at the property and the tenant paid his balance, both confirmed. ⭐ THAT MAKES THE CALL EASIER, NOT UNNECESSARY — what she actually asked is still unanswered: is the tenant out, because he owes another month if he is not. ⭐ YOU DO NOT NEED THE ANSWER TO MAKE THE CALL, and waiting for one is exactly what turned six days into twenty-three. ⭐ She is not a loose end — she closed with you in June and still opens your market reports.

callBlock.who: Claire C. — buyer from Saturday, and the phone is the ONLY way to reach her
callBlock.why: 🆕 SHE REGISTERED SATURDAY EARLY AFTERNOON and the machine handled her end to end in four minutes: ownership verified, first touch sent — and it hard-bounced one second later. ⚠️ HER EMAIL IS AN APPLE PRIVATE-RELAY ADDRESS, the third time this exact pattern has been confirmed on this desk. There is no email path to her at all, now or ever. ⭐ THAT MAKES THIS A DIFFERENT KIND OF TASK FROM THE REST OF THE LIST — every other name here can be worked two ways. This one cannot, and she is now roughly two days old, well past the window where speed-to-lead is worth anything.

callBlock.who: Anonymous call-in lead — a real person phoned the CRM Friday and nobody has called back
callBlock.why: ☎️ A HUMAN DIALLED YOUR NUMBER FRIDAY AFTERNOON. The record carries no name and no email — the phone is the only channel that exists, so this one genuinely cannot be worked any other way. ⚠️ THE ALERT SAT UNREAD FROM FRIDAY EVENING UNTIL SATURDAY MORNING'S SWEEP FOUND IT, and that is the whole cost here: an inbound phone call is the highest-intent lead type on the board and this one is now three days cold. ⭐ Ownership is verified as yours at the strong rung, so there is no question about whether it is your lead to work.

callBlock.who: Angela B. and Cassie C. — the two agents who called Comanche too high and still have not been told it came down
callBlock.why: 🔴 BOTH CHIPS ARE NOW EIGHT DAYS OVERDUE AND LAST NIGHT MADE THE CASE STRONGER. Cassie's buyer toured 7/25, wrote the offer and called the old ask too high; Angela's buyer toured 8/2, said interested YES and called the same old ask too high. Neither knows the price moved. 🆕 A THIRD AGENT FILED A YES ON SATURDAY NIGHT AND DID NOT ARGUE THE NUMBER — that is now five consecutive reads since the cut where nobody has written down a different price. ⭐ The pricing question on this house is settled; what is not settled is that two agents with interested buyers are still working off a dead number. ⛔ Quote the current list price only, and call rather than email — co-op agents are the red lane under your own rule, and that rule is exactly what the fleet is still waiting on you to revisit, now nine days.

callBlock.who: Alex T. — 521 property views, met with you once, and nobody has called in nine months
callBlock.why: ⚠️ THE QUIETEST EXPENSIVE MISS ON THE LIST. Five hundred and twenty-one property views is not browsing, it is somebody working a decision on their own for months — and the CRM stage says you have already met with him, which means the relationship exists and simply stopped. ⭐ NINE MONTHS OF SILENCE AFTER AN IN-PERSON MEETING IS THE CHEAPEST KIND OF LOST BUSINESS, because the hard part was already done. ⏰ Two days overdue on the chip and roughly two hundred and seventy days overdue on the relationship — the second number is the one that matters. ⭐ No pitch needed on the first call; ask what happened and whether the plan changed.

listings.status: 📸 Coming to market $185K — the shoot is TOMORROW MORNING, photographer booked and seller told
listings.note: ⏰ THIS IS THE ITEM THAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS TOMORROW. Both halves closed today on your ruling at 12:14 — the photographer is booked and the seller has been told — after this board opened the day with it as the loudest red row: sellers asked in writing on 8/12 for a Monday shoot, day four had arrived, nothing was booked. ⭐ WORTH KEEPING BECAUSE IT IS A PROCESS LESSON, NOT JUST A WIN: the desk had staged a written note to the seller and then reversed itself once you confirmed you had told her directly. That reversal was printed rather than quietly dropped, which is the only way these boards stay trustworthy. ✅ EVERYTHING ELSE ON THIS FILE ALREADY WENT RIGHT: both sellers executed all seven documents Friday morning, she at 11:41 and he at 11:49, on three separate receipts, and the milestone engine fired this address for the first time in its life. 🔴 WHAT IS STILL OPEN AND LANDS TOMORROW WITH THE SHOOT: the MLS input prep behind it, and the half of this relationship nobody has ever worked. ⭐ Remember what she actually came in saying — very interested in a property AND about ready to list their own. This is the LIST half of a two-sided deal, the BUY half has never been touched, and your own words to her were 'want to look Monday?' — which is tomorrow. ⚠️ The $185,000 price is your own ruling and is quotable, but it still has no primary MLS source behind it.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $295K — top of a buyer's list, still uncalled nineteen hours later
listings.note: 🔥 THE BEST NEWS ON THE BOARD IS ALSO THE OLDEST UNWORKED THING ON IT. Amy G. of Ethos International filed at 11:24 Saturday night off that afternoon's 1:00 PM tour: interested — YES, staged 3, and in her own words her buyers have just started looking, really like the property, and have put it at the top of their list. Nineteen hours later the call has not been made. ⭐ SHE IS THE SAME AGENT WHO PHONED YOU FROM INSIDE THE HOUSE mid-showing, which means the channel is already warm — this is a returned call, not a cold approach. ✅ THE PRICING QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED AS FIRMLY AS FEEDBACK CAN ANSWER IT: she left BOTH price fields blank, making FIVE consecutive reads since the 8/5 cut where nobody argued the number. Every read that ever said TOO HIGH was filed while the ask was $299,000. A $4,000 experiment that worked — do not reopen price with this seller. 🔴 THE LIVE ITEM IS THE BASEMENT LIGHTS. She reported on the phone that they would not turn on; you answered the garage half by text at 4:16 and that half is closed. This half is not. ⭐ She scored staging a 3 and is the ONLY agent to score staging since the cut, so she is worth asking what she would change. 🔴 Two co-op agents who expressed buyer interest still do not know the price moved — both chips overdue since 8/8. ⛔ Quote $295,000 only. ⛔ Call, don't email. ⚠️ One older thread is still unanswered: the 8/10 agent asked in writing whether the ceiling stains came from a previous leak.

listings.status: ⚖️ Active $450K — the agreement reinstates TOMORROW and the decision is still unruled
listings.note: ⏰ THE DECISION LANDS TOMORROW AND IT IS STILL OPEN. Three independent sources read 8/17 — the CRM crawl, the Ops Board reminder, and the chip that first caught the conflict — so the agreement reinstates TOMORROW, not last Friday. This board printed 8/14 twice and was wrong both times; the correction is logged rather than quietly swapped. ⚠️ AND IT IS A REINSTATEMENT, NOT AN EXTENSION — that came from Don himself Saturday morning, along with the fact that Mrs Ann had not yet been asked as of that reply. That is now about thirty-three hours old with still no sighting of a signed document, the sixth consecutive pass with none. 🆕 CHANGED TONIGHT AND SAID PLAINLY: the buyer who phoned Thursday about the workshop and garage has been STOOD DOWN and his chip closed with a written reason rather than left to age. He was the strongest single argument for reinstating, so the case for it is now thinner than this board carried it all weekend — that is a real change in the picture, not a bookkeeping tidy-up. ⭐ THE PRICING PICTURE IS UNCHANGED: day 91, no price change since May, exactly one written offer all summer, the 8/11 full-price showing this board carried for two days NEVER HAPPENED by the agent's own admission, and Friday's tour ran and produced total silence. ⭐ Both feedback forms this house has ever produced left every price field blank — the objections were the upstairs bathroom and a compartmentalized interior. Nobody who walked it has ever named a different number. ⚠️ Quote $450,000 only until the sellers rule.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract $899K — closes THURSDAY, and it is the quietest high-risk file you have
listings.note: ⏰ FOUR DAYS OUT AND THIS IS THE NEAREST CLOSING ON THE BOARD. ✅ What is verified and good: the appraisal is complete and clean on the lender's own words, the repair addendum is fully executed, the septic inspection ran 8/4, and the closing invite matches the stored state on the engine's own check. ⭐ CLOSING IS THURSDAY 8/20 AT 3:00 PM at the closing attorney's office. 🆕 THE BROKERAGE ISSUED THE COMMISSION DOCUMENT SATURDAY MORNING — the step three separate reminders had been chasing. That starts the payment clock on the largest number closing this month. ⚠️ THE HONEST WORRY IS THE SILENCE, NOT A PROBLEM — this desk has called it the quietest high-risk file in the book all week and nothing has come in since. Four days out with no traffic is worth one confirmation call to the attorney rather than an assumption, and tomorrow is the day to make it. ⛔ The old 8/14 close date is retired — do not re-print it anywhere. ⭐ One thing worth having ready: a closing this size is the strongest referral moment you will get this month, and the review-ask on the last funded closing is still sitting untouched at twenty-seven days.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $550K — two showings in one Saturday, and still not one word back
listings.note: 🆕 TWO SEPARATE AGENTS WALKED THIS HOUSE ON SATURDAY, SIX HOURS APART — one at 11:10 in the morning and one at 4:00 in the afternoon, taking the all-time counter from 41 to 42 in a single day. ✅ THE SOURCE PROBLEM THIS BOARD FLAGGED FOR TWO DAYS IS CLOSED: both notices print the list price at $550,000. Every prior notice on file printed $559,000 because they all predated the cut, so the price was one source seen repeatedly. It is now confirmed independently and it is quotable. ⭐ THE TIMING IS THE POINT — the cut went live 8/13 and produced two tours inside forty-eight hours on a house whose last read called it too high. That is the market answering the question directly. 🔴 NEITHER TOUR HAS FILED FEEDBACK AND BOTH ARE NOW PAST A FULL DAY, AND THE 8/10 TOUR BEFORE THEM NEVER DID EITHER — three showings deep with nothing returned, which is the single biggest information gap on the board. 🔴 THE ITEM THIS BOARD HAS CARRIED UNACTIONED FOR THREE WEEKS IS STILL THE ONE THAT WOULD MOVE THE NEEDLE: the 7/23 read said dirty plus GLITCHING ELECTRICAL, and the 8/4 read scored staging 2 of 5, the lowest this listing has ever recorded, against a 4 three weeks earlier from an agent who called the price JUST RIGHT. The house did not get more expensive between those visits — it got less presentable. ✅ The marketing lane caught the unpublished cut this morning and staged the corrected creative for the week ahead — the live 8/10 post still carries $559,000 until it is approved.

listings.status: 🎉 Under contract $390,000 — the response WENT OUT, and the draft still in the folder is a duplicate
listings.note: ✅ CORRECTION WORTH READING, BECAUSE THIS BOARD HAD IT WRONG TWICE. The inspection-response letter to the sellers was NOT sitting unsent — you sent it yourself Saturday morning at 9:54. The document still sitting in the drafts folder is a DUPLICATE created six minutes later, and it is flagged for deletion rather than aging as pending follow-up. Two separate reads called it 'unsent for 24 hours'; both were reading the copy, not the original. ⚠️ It is now roughly thirty-two hours old and still nothing has deleted it — a hazard, not a task, and the only untidy thing in an otherwise clean drafts folder. ⭐ THE SHAPE OF THE ASK IS THE STORY AND IT IS GOOD NEWS: they inspected seventy-one items, flagged sixty-eight at some level, and then asked for exactly three. That is a reasonable buyer. ⭐ THE RECOMMENDATION YOU SENT IS TWO YESES AND A HOLD — agree to the basement leak and to a scoped HVAC service, and on the roof do not say no, say give us a few days and our own licensed roofer's report. The inspector wrote in the same section that he cannot determine the roof's age or remaining life, which is the report itself saying the roof question is unanswered. ⚠️ TWO THINGS BEFORE FIGHTING THE ROOF: this is FHA, so the appraiser can raise it independently, and the concession room left under the FHA cap is small, so this gets solved with work rather than a check. ✅ The sellers have acknowledged the roof-holdback approach. ⭐ Closing 10/23 — roughly ten weeks, which is a luxury most files do not get.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract — both gates cleared, close 8/28, and the seller is still waiting on a call
listings.note: ✅ STILL THE CLEANEST FILE ON YOUR BOARD ON PAPER. Both gates are behind you: the inspection ran 8/5 at noon and the appraisal 8/7 at 9:00 AM, both on primary notices, and the 8/28 close date was cross-checked against three sources again this evening and passed. ⭐ AN INSPECTION AND AN APPRAISAL BOTH SPENT IS THE STRONGEST POSITION ANY DEAL ON THIS BOARD OCCUPIES. ✅ AND THE ONE THING THAT COULD HAVE BITTEN IT GOT CAUGHT WITHOUT YOU: your operations manager chased and closed the payoff item on 8/14, with two status comments on the record. That is the catch that protects the close, and it is worth acknowledging to her. 🔴 AND YET THE SELLER HAS BEEN WAITING ON A RETURNED CALL SINCE TUESDAY — five days now, mid-transaction, on the deal with the least to worry about. That is the row on this file that needs you, and tomorrow is Client Day. ⚠️ The appraised value still has not come back — day ten, reported as a single-source observation rather than an alarm, and worth one call to the lender. ⚠️ One number remains unruled and it is worth real money on an otherwise settled deal: the buyer's agent asked for a specific co-op commission and nobody has ever answered.

listings.status: 🎉 Under contract $162K — inspection held, both price reads validated the number
listings.note: ✅ THE FIRST GATE IS BEHIND YOU — inspection confirmed and held 8/13 at 10:00 AM; MLS reads CONTINGENT. ✅ THE PAPERWORK ITEM IS CLOSED, NOT PENDING: the contract went out with all signatures, the contract-to-close packet reached title 8/12, and the closing attorney confirmed receipt. ⚠️ ONE THREAD THAT IS NOT CLOSED: the executed contract has been with your operations manager since Tuesday and five days have now passed without a status back. On a file this clean that is a process gap rather than a deal risk, but it is the kind that becomes a deal risk quietly — and it is one of two items on her board waiting to be read back. ⭐ TWO INDEPENDENT READS NOW VALIDATE THIS PRICE — the agent who wrote the offer called it JUST RIGHT, and a late form off the 8/7 tour said interested No but PRICED JUST RIGHT with a staging 3 of 5. That is the kind of evidence that matters if anything wobbles before 9/14. ⭐ THE BACKSTORY IS WORTH KEEPING ON THE RECORD: the buyer's agent said her client really liked it but needed to save more for a down payment, and this desk argued for two weeks against reading that as a price signal — she had written JUST RIGHT on the same form. She wrote. Offer to acceptance in twenty-eight minutes. Patience was the right call. ⭐ Closing 9/14.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $184K — a 'VERY interested' buyer is now eight days unworked
listings.note: 🔥 THE LISTING THIS BOARD ONCE CALLED INVISIBLE PRODUCED THREE TOURS IN A SINGLE SATURDAY, all three forms filed within ninety minutes of each other on 8/8. One answered the interest question with the single word "Very" and left every other field blank — which is exactly why it needs a phone call: the enthusiasm is on record and the reason is not. ✅ THE $5,000 CUT IS VERIFIED LIVE AND PUBLIC — the MLS line on all three notices reads $184,000, so the old do-not-quote hedge is retired. 🔴 THE REAL FINDING IS THE OBJECTION AND IT IS VERIFIED THREE WAYS: the problem is SIZE, not price. The clearest read says it in four words — "Just too small." ⛔ NO DISCOUNT REACHES A SIZE OBJECTION. The answer here is AUDIENCE — first-time buyers, downsizers, investors — and a price conversation with this seller would be solving the wrong problem. This board argued for a cut here for weeks on the strength of silence; the showings arrived and said something different, and that earlier read is withdrawn. 🔴 That Saturday burst has now fully decayed with the one phone call still unmade.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $599K package — a SEVENTH name came off the ad today, and the septic answer is still undelivered
listings.note: 🆕 THE AD PRODUCED AGAIN THIS AFTERNOON — a new buyer came off the 19-lot listing and then registered on your IDX site four minutes later, which is a materially stronger signal than either channel alone. That makes seven names off this one ad while every other ad in the portfolio produced zero. ✅ THE DELIVERABLE WAS LOCATED FRIDAY MORNING — the 19-lot plat, which is precisely what the open buyer chip had been waiting on since he answered "Yes", and it went out the same morning. 🔴 THE THING THAT SHOULD BOTHER YOU MOST ON THIS FILE IS NOT THE COUNTY, IT IS THE HANDOFF: the builder asked the septic perc question on 8/12, your operations manager researched and answered it completely, and that answer has been sitting on her board since Friday with nobody reading it back to him. Day four. The work was done; the delivery never happened. ⭐ THE PERC QUESTION ITSELF IS PRICED RATHER THAN BLOCKED: the county takes record searches in person only, weekdays 8:00 to 3:30, at a per-record fee — across nineteen lots that is a four-figure errand. ⭐ SO THE CHOICE IS THREE-WAY, NOT TWO: send someone for all nineteen, narrow the pull to the lots a buyer is actually asking about, or try the free path first and ask the developer, who almost certainly already holds the perc results from platting. ⭐ PERC DECIDES BUILDABILITY AND BUILDABILITY DECIDES PRICE PER LOT, which is why this one question governs the whole package. ⚠️ Two builder outreach addresses hard-bounced permanently after 48 hours of retries — part of the builder audience received nothing at all, and those two need replacing rather than resending.

listings.status: 🔴 Active — sixteen days quiet, and the good news is STILL undelivered
listings.note: 🔴 TWO TOURS IN FIVE DAYS AT THE END OF JULY, THEN NOTHING SINCE. On a listing that had gone 126 days with essentially no traffic, that brief burst was the only real activity this file has produced and it has fully decayed. ⭐ THE GOOD NEWS IS STILL UNDELIVERED AT SIXTEEN DAYS, WHICH MAKES IT THE OLDEST OWED ITEM ON THE BOARD: the 7/31 read came back interested No, but with the price called JUST RIGHT, a 4 of 5 rating, and the comment that the buyers prefer the east end of the beach although they liked this complex. That is a GEOGRAPHY loss, not a price loss, and it is the only independent validation of this list price the file has ever carried. ⚠️ AND IT HAS NOW SLID OUT OF THE FOURTEEN-DAY WINDOW — as of today that read no longer appears in the rolling feedback count on the showing board. The finding is not gone, but the clock on delivering it has run out of runway. ⭐ He is out of state and lives on these reads — lead with the price answer, not the no. ⚠️ A price discrepancy opened during the dark window and is still unresolved: two sources five thousand apart, and neither is quotable until the MLS is read directly.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active $1.15M — biggest listing in the book, seller identity STILL unverified
listings.note: ⚠️ THE LARGEST NUMBER ON YOUR BOARD IS STILL THE ONE WITH THE WEAKEST FILE. No showing, no feedback and no correspondence has crossed this desk on this address in the fourteen-day window. ⛔ THE CLIENT IDENTITY REMAINS UNVERIFIED under the identity law — a name is carried in memory, and memory is not a receipt. On a $1.15M listing that is not a formality: it gates every piece of client-facing creative and every seller email. ⭐ THE POSITIONING READ IS STILL THE MOST USEFUL THING ON THE FILE: the only tour this listing ever took said, verbatim, that the buyer liked the house but the land wasn't what he was looking for. The objection is ACREAGE — which at this price point is the cheapest possible loss, because nobody has ever said it is too expensive. ⭐ THE UNANSWERED QUESTION IS THEREFORE A TARGETING ONE: who is the buyer who wants THIS land, and is the marketing pointed at them. 🆕 The engagement sweep found four stale hands-up on this address's social posts today and raised them as their own task — that is the only inbound interest this listing has produced in two weeks. ⏰ The 8/2 open house was never debriefed and its sign-in sheet was never captured — two weeks on, that is effectively lost. 🛑 The lookalike meeting link on this address is still not to be opened, on any device.

listings.status: ⚠️ Active — price cut to $285K on 8/11, and the live ad still shows the old number
listings.note: ⚠️ A PRICE CUT THAT THE MARKETING NEVER HEARD ABOUT, NOW ON DAY SIX. The listing came down to $285,000 on 8/11 per the CRM's own field, while an 8/8 social post that is still live carries $289,900. ⭐ THAT IS A CHEAP FIX AND A REAL ONE — a public ad quoting a dead number is the kind of small inconsistency buyers and agents actually notice, and it makes every other number you publish slightly less trustworthy. ⚠️ IT IS ALSO NOT THE ONLY ONE: Ridge Trail has the identical problem. Two live ads quoting two dead prices is no longer a one-off, it is a publishing gap. ✅ THE FIX IS NOW STAGED RATHER THAN THEORETICAL — this morning's marketing blitz wrote the full week-of-8/17 plan and loaded eight placements into an empty queue, with the corrected pricing in them. It is one approval tomorrow, not a project. ⚠️ THIS IS TWO ARTIFACTS RATHER THAN TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES, so it is printed as a waiting-on-you item rather than a red flag: the CRM field and the live post disagree, and the MLS has not been read directly to break the tie.

listings.status: 🔴 Active — the tenant answer is twenty-three days owed
listings.note: 🔴 THE LONGEST-RUNNING BROKEN PROMISE ON THE BOARD, AND IT FINALLY BROKE HER PATIENCE. She left a twenty-two-second voicemail on 7/25 rather than sending a seventh text — which is what a patient client does when nothing comes back — and then on Wednesday night she escalated THREE TIMES IN TWENTY-SEVEN MINUTES: two voicemails and a text. ✅ THE EMERGENCY HALF RESOLVED WITHOUT YOU — power is back on at the property and the tenant paid his balance, both confirmed this week. ⭐ THE OWED THING IS STILL YOURS: she asked whether the tenant on this unit is out, because he owes another month's rent if he isn't. ⚠️ YOU DO NOT NEED AN ANSWER TO MAKE THIS CALL. "Still no word from him, here's exactly what I'm doing about it" beats a twenty-fourth day of silence. ⭐ She is not a loose end — she closed with you in June, still opens your market reports, and has an unclosed valuation loop on this same address.

listings.status: 🆕 Buyer-side pending — long fuse, one answer owed
listings.note: 🆕 REAL GCI THE FORECAST COULD NOT SEE UNTIL LAST WEEK — roughly $44.6K across this address and a second buyer-side file, both weighted at zero in every prior model. That is not new business; it is business you already had that the system was blind to. ⭐ ONE LIVE OPEN ITEM AND IT IS NOW MORE THAN TWO WEEKS OLD: a builder change-order and pre-qualification message, deliberately left in the inbox rather than filed because it is the only thing on this file that wants an answer. ⚠️ Long fuse — it closes late January 2027 with a production builder — so the change order is the only item carrying urgency, and two weeks of silence on a builder question is how change orders get decided without you.

listings.status: 🔴 Buyer-side $2.35M — the counter has never been put on paper, day 26
listings.note: 🔴 THE LARGEST SINGLE NUMBER ON YOUR BOARD, ROUGHLY $36K OF GCI, AND THE WHOLE COST OF MOVING IT IS TWENTY MINUTES OF WRITING. The listing side has asked repeatedly since 7/21 to be moved forward and has never received a written position from your side. ⚠️ STATED HONESTLY: a phone call leaves no receipt, so this is ABSENCE rather than proven failure — but what was promised was paper, and there is none on any lane this desk can read. ⭐ WHY IT KEEPS RETURNING: a seller who reverse-offers a buyer is a seller who wants a deal, and the honest answer IS the counter.
